Four of the five Schedule B sheets close EXACTLY on their own printed subtotals: p3's 15 rows sum to 724.22, p4's 15 to 152.03, p6's 15 to 259.77 and p7's 2 to 47.19. Page 5's 15 rows sum to 216.56 against its printed subtotal of 216.47, so the whole discrepancy is on that sheet, and the side totals 1,399.77 against the printed 1,399.68 / Box D. THE OFFENDING ROW IS UNIQUELY IDENTIFIED, by the filer's own arithmetic and not by guesswork. This filer's mileage rows are computed as miles x $0.585 (he prints the rate in the very first one, 'Cottage Meeting - Cedar Fort, 48 miles x .585'), and EVERY other mileage cell on page 5 reproduces that formula to the cent: 20 mi -> 11.70 (three times), 10 -> 5.85, 66 -> 38.61, 19 -> 11.12, 6 -> 3.51, 40 -> 23.40, 44 -> 25.74, 12 -> 7.02, 50 -> 29.25, 9 -> 5.27. The row is retained verbatim at 8.87 and flagged. The whole p5 amount column was additionally re-rendered at 900 dpi and every one of the fifteen cells reproduced as recorded, and the doubled-band screen (ADDENDUM H3) passed on all five sheets — each measured band rendered exactly one figure — so the shortfall is not a missed or collapsed row.
